purpose: Verify that removing either new helper-family lowering fails a runtime reachability assertion instead of silently passing through interpreter fallback.
sourceProvenance: Mutations ran on the pre-commit working tree that became the reference revision. The PS mutation preceded a diagnostic-only change of two admission assertion messages from "must be emitted inline" to "must be admitted"; the final restored-source run used the committed reference revision. No lowering or reachability-assertion behavior changed between mutation runs and that commit.

procedure: Use an isolated checkout of sourceRevision and a caller-supplied persistent scratch directory.
Apply exactly one literal replacement below to the named file, starting from pristine source each time. Admission policy and runtime counter assertions stay enabled.
Set TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP to that persistent scratch directory. Run the command below and require exit code 1 plus the stated assertion.
Restore the file before applying the other mutation. Restore all source and rerun the same command to require the final passing summary.
reproduction.compilerPolicy: The test script sources tools/wasm-rustflags.sh from the pinned revision.

limitations: Each mutation aborts on its first failing assertion, so it does not complete the full suite.
This checks detection of deleted lowerings, not mutation coverage for every possible semantic defect.
Raw logs are not independently accessible from the published repository; the exact mutations, reproduction command, failure assertions and original log hashes are retained.

privacy.curation: Private local build paths and raw stack traces were omitted. Exact failure messages, result counts and original raw-log hashes were preserved.
